title: Stratus API authentication breakthrough - auth cache discovery
summary: Debugged and resolved Stratus API integration authentication issues by discovering OpenClaw's dual auth storage (config + cache). API now authenticating successfully with 17784 credits confirmed. Identified next blocker: role field compatibility.
detail: AUTHENTICATION BREAKTHROUGH: After extensive debugging, discovered that OpenClaw maintains TWO separate locations for API authentication: (1) Config file ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (what users edit) and (2) Auth cache ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json (what the gateway actually uses). The config file does NOT automatically sync to the auth cache, causing silent failures. Solution: Updated auth cache with Stratus credentials, restarted gateway (openclaw gateway restart), verified with curl. Results: API endpoint dev.api.stratus.run responding correctly, API key validated, user balance confirmed at 17784.00 credits, model stratus-x1ac-base-claude-sonnet-4-5 available. NEW BLOCKER DISCOVERED: Role field incompatibility - OpenClaw sends 'role: developer' (Anthropic-specific) but Stratus/Anthropic expects 'role: user' or 'role: assistant' when using OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Error: 'messages: Unexpected role developer. Allowed roles are user or assistant'. Next step: Implement role mapping in plugin (developer → system) to achieve compatibility.
learned: OpenClaw has dual auth storage: config file + auth cache (auth-profiles.json)
Config changes don't auto-sync to auth cache - must update both manually
Auth cache staleness causes silent fallback to other providers
401 errors indicate auth cache issue, not endpoint issue
Always verify auth independently with curl before debugging plugin code
The 'developer' role is Anthropic-specific and not supported in OpenAI-compatible APIs
incomplete: Chat completion test with role mapping
next: Implement role mapping in src/client.ts: normalizeRole() function to transform developer → system before API calls

title: Stratus OpenClaw Plugin - Official Integration Complete
summary: Successfully published Stratus X1-AC plugin to npm as @formthefog/stratus. Complete integration includes 75 models, 2 tools, bundled knowledge skill, enhanced documentation, and GTM materials. Plugin is production-ready and installable via 'openclaw plugins install @formthefog/stratus'.
detail: MAJOR MILESTONE: Completed full integration of Stratus X1-AC world model into OpenClaw ecosystem. Started with package naming issues and installation failures, systematically resolved all blockers: (1) Fixed package naming convention (@hathbanger/openclaw-stratus → @hathbanger/stratus → @formthefog/stratus to match plugin ID), (2) Resolved folder extraction mismatch, (3) Fixed non-interactive setup command (removed prompter dependency, uses env vars), (4) Added comprehensive security manifest documenting credential access, (5) Created bundled /stratus-info skill with full technical knowledge base explaining JEPA architecture and world model capabilities, (6) Enhanced provider registration notes to educate users during auth setup, (7) Migrated to @formthefog npm organization, (8) Deprecated old packages with migration notices, (9) Updated all documentation and GTM materials, (10) Posted GitHub issue update requesting @openclaw org access. Final package includes 14 files (16.3KB README, 5.7KB skill, 14.3KB index), published as v2026.2.19. GTM materials updated via agent collaboration including product overview, ecosystem strategy, launch announcement, and 4-week launch checklist. Integration represents official Stratus distribution channel through OpenClaw's 10K+ user base.
learned: OpenClaw plugin naming must match plugin ID (folder name from npm package extraction must equal plugin ID in manifest)
Command handlers don't have access to prompter object - interactive prompts only work in auth flows
Skills can be bundled with plugins by adding skills/ directory and referencing in openclaw.plugin.json
Provider registration notes are shown during auth setup and should explain architecture, not just features
Security manifests via code comments help reduce/explain security scanner warnings
npm org migration requires deprecating old packages, updating all docs, and notifying community via issues/announcements
GTM materials should be updated immediately when new distribution channels launch
Peer service agents can update sibling repos when provided proper context and file paths
next: Monitor plugin adoption metrics, collect user feedback, prepare for @openclaw org migration when access granted, create integration walkthrough video, publish launch announcement across channels

title: Updated API endpoint configuration to production
summary: Changed all references from dev.api.stratus.run to api.stratus.run across the entire codebase to use the production Stratus API endpoint.
detail: Comprehensively updated all configuration files, source code, documentation, and scripts to use the production API endpoint (api.stratus.run) instead of the development endpoint (dev.api.stratus.run). This included: 1) Core source files (src/config.ts, src/client.ts, index.ts, src/setup.ts) updated with new default baseUrl, 2) Configuration files (openclaw.plugin.json) updated with new default endpoint, 3) Installation scripts (install.sh) updated to configure production endpoint, 4) All documentation (README.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md, knowledge/INTEGRATION_STATUS.md, skills/stratus-info/SKILL.md) updated with production endpoint examples, 5) Service status file (.jfl/status.json) updated to reflect production-ready status. The production API deployment is now stable and fully functional after recent fixes.

learned: Production API endpoint is now stable and ready for use
Dev endpoint should no longer be referenced in any configuration
Comprehensive update across 11 files ensures consistent configuration
